STATES: u0, u1, u2, u3, u4
INITIAL_STATE: u0
FINAL_STATES: u4
TRANSITION_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key) -> u1
(u0, else) -> u0
(u1, blocker_moved & has_door_key) -> u2
(u1, else) -> u1
(u2, door_open & has_door_key) -> u3
(u2, else) -> u2
(u3, target_picked_up) -> u4
(u3, else) -> u3
(u4, else) -> u4
REWARD_FUNCTION:
(u0, blocker_moved & !has_door_key, u1) -> 0.1
(u1, blocker_moved & has_door_key, u2) -> 0.1
(u2, door_open & has_door_key, u3) -> 0.1
(u3, target_picked_up, u4) -> 1.0
feedback: ACCEPTED. The RM is a faithful, minimal encoding of the task order 'ball -> key -> door -> box'. Verified points: (1) Semantic fidelity/order: u0->u1 requires blocker_moved with !has_door_key, so the key-first flow (pick key, drop key firing key_lost, then move ball) earns nothing until the ball is moved while unholding the key, and u1->u2 requires blocker_moved & has_door_key simultaneously, so the key only counts as 'taken' while the ball is away — enforcing 'move the ball before you take the key'. The chain u1->u2->u3 plus the physical constraint (toggle needs the matching key in hand) enforces key-before-door; u3->u4 (target_picked_up, physically impossible before door_open) enforces door-before-box. (2) Reachability: u4 is reachable exactly along the seed-0 trace — +0.1 at step 4 (u0->u1), +0.1 at step 12 (u1->u2), +0.1 at step 17 (u2->u3, fires on the toggle step since has_door_key still holds), +1.0 at step 28; the step-19 key drop keeps key_lost false (door open) and is absorbed by the u3 else-loop. (3) Compactness: 5 states / 4 progress transitions is minimal for 4 ordered subgoals. (4) Predicate-only events: all guards use only the five given propositions; no invented predicates; key_lost is correctly left unused by guards and covered by per-state else self-loops (it can only fire with the door closed, i.e., in u0/u1/u2, where it is absorbed without wrong transitions). (5) Persistent/event distinction: conditions are re-checked each step via simultaneous guards; the event key_lost is never latched. (6) Regression handling: blocker_moved and has_door_key can revert (ball dropped back, key dropped), and the guards handle this correctly — the RM waits at u1/u2 until both conditions coincide again, and door_open cannot revert (no relock), so no explicit regression transitions are required; the agent is never stuck in any state. (7) Reward safety: forward-only chain, each transition fires at most once, total bounded at 1.3 with per-step <= 1.0; dense progress shaping (0.1 per stage) plus 1.0 terminal; no negative or farmable rewards. (8) Format: REWARD_MACHINE/STATES/INITIAL_STATE/FINAL_STATES/TRANSITION_FUNCTION/REWARD_FUNCTION headers all present in the paper format; FINAL_STATES is nonempty (u4), u4 is declared in STATES and accepting (absorbing else self-loop, terminal for the task). Minor harmless redundancies (not defects): the !has_door_key conjunct on u0->u1 and the has_door_key conjunct on u2->u3 are implied by the one-object carrying constraint and one-transition-per-step semantics, but they document the intended order explicitly. Note the candidate correctly uses blocker_moved (per environment.md) rather than the published RM's stricter has_ball, as instructed by task-rm-pairs.md.

All five environment-declared propositions are implemented and there are no extra functions; key_lost is unused in the RM but is a declared predicate and correctly required. blocker_moved locates the unique door and reports true iff the cell (dx-1, dy) holds no ball, matching the reference single-cell reading: a ball in hand counts as moved, and dropping the ball back onto that cell flips it false again. The door-scan formulation differs structurally from the reference lookup but is semantically identical given exactly one door and the fixed ball cell (dx-1, dy) from _gen_grid; the door is never at x=0, so the x-1 lookup is always in range and Grid.get out-of-bounds returns None regardless. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented expressions exactly (carrying a key whose color equals a door's color, any open door, carrying the box named by env.mission). key_lost has correct event semantics: it reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only, requiring has_door_key true at the previous step and false now with door_open false now, exactly prev['has_door_key'] and not K and not D; the bool(...) guard is harmless since a falsy valuation implies the event is false anyway. Persistent propositions use only current state and only the event touches the previous-valuation snapshot. Only documented API surface is used (grid.get with None guards, carrying, mission, width, height, object type/color/is_open, previous_valuation); no imports, no actions, no mutation of env or episode memory; syntax is valid Python.
